$comment: Victron Venus plugin configuration. The Cerbo GX is reached over plain MQTT on the boat network; the simulator's emulated Cerbo answers on the same protocol, so this file is identical on the boat and on the bench apart from the host. Instance mappings give a device a stable Signal K name, otherwise its paths carry the raw Victron instance number, which can change if the device is reset or swapped. The battery mapping below is not a guess: read directly off Cinderella's real Cerbo on 2026-08-14 by subscribing to its MQTT topic tree (com.victronenergy.battery, instance 279, a BMV-712 Smart on VE.Direct). A Multiplus (com.victronenergy.vebus, instance 276) was confirmed live on 2026-08-24 by querying the freshly-provisioned boat Pi's own Signal K REST API (GET /signalk/v1/api/vessels/self/electrical) and reading the raw instance number back from the unmapped path — this is the same unit the physical panel's charger/inverter LEDs belong to, including the mains LED that electrical.chargers.main.leds.mains now exposes. There is no solar charger connected to this Cerbo — confirmed the same way, not merely quiet — so no mapping is given for it; the simulator still emits synthetic solar data (for testing the marina/anchored dashboards), which will appear under its own raw instance number rather than a named path until real hardware exists to map. Add an entry here the same way these were found: either subscribe to N/+/+/# and publish an empty message to R/<portalId>/system/0/Serial to prompt a state dump, or — simpler once Signal K is already running — GET its REST API and read the instance number back from whatever unmapped path shows up.
